title: Polaris AI - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Intro discovery to understand Polaris AI's networking constraints for a Private/VPC deployment. Main topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints (EU data residency), private endpoints, routing/NAT, EKS cross-account access, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 requirements. Agreed next steps: share architecture diagram, security docs, schedule technical deep dive and internal procurement sync.
topics: Latency/cost tradeoffs between Dedicated and Private
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-29 15:30 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Jesse Carter, Maya Singh (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Priya Natarajan, Diego Ramos (Polaris AI)

[00:00] Jesse: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jesse from redwood, i'll kick us off. we have maya our solution engineer too.
[00:06] Liam: thanks, yeah appreciate you making time. quick context, we're evaluating options for running inference for our customer-facing agents, and security/regulatory is the blocker \u0014 we need private connectivity and eu data residency.
[00:18] Maya: great, can you run through existing infra \u0014 vpc setup, accounts, cloud provider, any transit gateways?
[00:24] Priya: we run in aws, multiple accounts under org polaris-prod and polaris-dev. primary region eu-west-1 for customer data. we have an aws transit gateway for some cross-account routing, and our EKS clusters live in private subnets. the ask is a private deployment of redwood, ideally inside our vpc or peered, with kms keys we control.
[00:39] Jesse: ok makes sense. when you say \"inside our vpc or peered\", are you picturing dedicated nodes you manage, or a private deployment where redwood runs a control plane managed by them but compute in your vpc?
[00:48] Liam: prefer control over compute. we want the inference instances to live in our account for audit and egress control. but open to options if redwood can guarantee isolation and logs.
[00:58] Maya: two patterns we typically discuss: 1) private deployment where the customer hosts both control and data plane in their vpc (on-prem or VPC), 2) a managed private where control plane is hosted, compute runs in customer account via peering or private endpoints. each has tradeoffs for ops overhead.
[01:15] Diego: from security we need BYOK support \u0014 keys never leave our custody. also need detailed audit logs, and SOC2 plus an iso attestation. can you share those docs?
[01:24] Jesse: absolutely, we'll send SOC2 and our security pack. link to shared doc: https://redwood.example.com/security/polaris-pack (note: placeholder).
[01:32] Priya: great. networking: our security policy disallows internet-facing endpoints for inference traffic; we need private endpoints or peering. prefer aws PrivateLink over peering due to simpler security boundaries, but concerned about cross-AZ cost and latency. thoughts?
[01:46] Maya: sure. PrivateLink provides interface endpoints, keep traffic off the internet and it crosses AZs via AWS-managed infra. VPC peering is simpler but can get messy at scale and doesn't cross regions. for eu-west-1 specifically both work, but peering requires route table updates and careful CIDR planning.
[02:02] Liam: we also have a small footprint in eu-central-1 for DR; can redwood deploy instances there or do you require single-region?
[02:09] Maya: we can support multi-region private deployments; typically we recommend co-locating inference in the same region as the data for latency and residency. if you want active-active we'd coordinate a multi-region config and data sync considerations.
[02:21] Diego: what about transit gateway? we use a tgw for central connectivity. can redwood endpoints connect to our tgw?
[02:28] Jesse: yes, we support connecting via transit gateway, but requires a peering/attachment configuration on both sides. we have customers who attach interfaces to tgw or use VPC endpoints in the spoke accounts. we'll share an architecture doc with examples.
[02:41] Priya: any limits around CIDR overlap? we have some historic overlap in prod and staging which has bitten us before.
[02:47] Maya: we need unique CIDRs for peering; PrivateLink alleviates some overlap worries because it uses ENIs in your subnets, but you still need space for endpoints. we can discuss a hybrid \u0014 PrivateLink for control plane and peered VPC for heavy data plane if necessary.
[03:05] Liam: latency: our SLAs need 150ms p95 for short prompts. how does private compare to dedicated in terms of tail latency?
[03:13] Maya: Dedicated reserved capacity in Redwood Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower multi-tenant interference; private in your VPC can be equal or better if you provision GPUs accordingly. main differences are deployment topology and ops burden. we can run benchmarks with your sample prompts to validate p95.
[03:30] Diego: and egress \u0014 we need to control egress paths and NAT. if instances run in our private subnets, will outbound to the control plane or artifacts be forced through our NAT gateways?
[03:39] Jesse: yes, if compute is in your account typical egress follows your routing (NAT or IGW) unless you use interface endpoints for S3 or private links for control plane. we support S3 VPC endpoints for model artifacts and private DNS.
[03:51] Priya: model artifacts \u0014 do we need to pull large models from redwood, or can we seed them locally? we want to avoid large cross-region pulls during deploys.
[03:58] Maya: you can bring your own model artifacts into your S3 and we support image-based deployment, also we provide a secure transfer flow for initial sync. we can discuss staging via a signed transfer or aws s3 replication.
[04:10] Liam: compliance wise, do you support HSM/KMS integration? we need keys in our KMS and hardware module for some customers.
[04:17] Maya: BYOK to customer-managed KMS is supported for secrets and signing in our private deployments; HSM integration varies by cloud and region but we have a flow to bring keys and manage rotation. we'll include the KMS/HSM guide.
[04:28] Diego: what about private DNS? our services use internal hostnames; endpoint discovery must not rely on public DNS.
[04:33] Jesse: we support private DNS for interface endpoints and provide a host file/route53 private zone instructions for automatic resolution. there may be small discrepancies in auto-generated cert CNs; we can walk through that in engineering call.
[04:46] Priya: traffic inspection \u0014 we do IDS/IPS on egress. will redwood require sidecars or can we integrate with network firewall?
[04:53] Maya: if compute in your account, you can apply your existing network controls; we don't require sidecars. if we host control plane then traffic would go to our endpoints and you'd need to allowlist those.
[05:02] Liam: okay, that's helpful. question on deployment time \u0014 how long does a private deployment typically take to spin up?
[05:08] Maya: depends on size and compliance checks \u0014 a small pilot can be up in 2-3 days (provisioning and security review), full production often 2-4 weeks because of audits, KMS setup, network approvals.
[05:18] Diego: procurement question \u0014 do you have standard enterprise contracts and can we do a pilot clause?
[05:22] Jesse: yes we have enterprise terms, can include a pilot schedule. we'll forward a template.
[05:27] Priya: any competitors mentioned? we did look at Anthropic/Claude and OpenAI private options, also a self-hosted vendor.
[05:34] Jesse: noted. Anthropic and OpenAI private endpoints were mentioned earlier in our notes too.
[05:38] Maya: one technical caveat \u0014 if you require cross-region replication of KV caches for low latency across eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 that adds complexity and potential consistency tradeoffs. we recommend regional pinning for low-latency inference.
[05:52] Liam: that makes sense. next steps? i'd like a technical deep dive with our infra team and a pricing/contract chat with procurement.
[05:59] Jesse: proposed next steps: we'll share security pack and architecture diagrams, schedule a SE deep dive (with Maya) next week, and send draft pricing for a 3-month pilot. also arrange a short benchmark run with your sample prompts.
[06:12] Priya: can you include a sample network diagram for PrivateLink + TGW and for compute-in-customer-account?
[06:17] Maya: yes, i'll attach two diagrams.
[06:20] Diego: timeline: target pilot start mid-jan.
[06:23] Jesse: noted. i'll follow up with times.
[06:26] Liam: ok thanks, that's it from me.
[06:28] Jesse: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and scheduler.
